blocks.text: My Lord, we're going to deal with searches this afternoon with the exhibits officer. By way of introduction I'm going to read six fairly, I hope, straightforward admissions. They are not yet in writing because they form part of a larger bundle of admissions which haven't been finalised yet. With your Lordship's leave I'll simply read them, the defence are content for me to do that, just before I call DC Johnson.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Of course, yes. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (In the presence of the jury)

I've received two notes from the jurors about sitting day difficulties. What I am going to do is put those on one side for the moment and review with counsel, first of all, the known days we are not sitting, raise these, and then just come back to you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I've received these requests, I'll obviously accommodate them, but you'll appreciate we're getting more and more intermittent now and each day we lose just adds more and more time further down the line, which therefore means there's more likely to be further interruptions later on.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: But I'll deal with these later and we'll prepare a comprehensive list. It may not be today. We'll sit until 4.20 or thereabouts this afternoon. We'll have perhaps a slightly shorter lunch. Is three-quarters of an hour long enough for a lunch break for you? I don't know if some of you have things to do.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Summary of agreed facts (read)
Thank you, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I'm going to begin this afternoon, please, with some agreed facts. They are not yet in writing, they will be very soon, but I read them at this stage because they hopefully set the scene for the evidence we're about to hear.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: They read as follows under the heading "Arrests".
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Number 26 in our list:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Lucy Letby was arrested on three occasions during the course of this investigation: (a) at her home address of 41 Westbourne Avenue, Chester, at 06.00 hours on 3 July 2018; (b) at her parents' home address in Hereford at 06.55 hours on 10 June 2019; (c) at her parents' home address in Hereford at 07.25 hours on 10 November 2020."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: You're going to get these in writing.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Make notes by all means, but you'll get them set out to add to the agreed facts.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: It's the dates that we want to flag up at this stage, thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Moving on to the heading of "Seizures", in 2018, agreed fact number 27:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Lucy Letby's home address at 41 Westbourne Avenue, Chester, was lawfully searched between the 3rd and 6 July 2018."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Number 28:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Lucy Letby's parents' home address of 13 Arran Avenue, Hereford was lawfully searched between the 3rd and 6 July 2018."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Number 29:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Lucy Letby's place of work at the risk department Mostyn Lodge at the Countess of Chester Hospital was lawfully searched between 10.15 hours and 11.50 hours on 3 July 2018."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Moving on to 2019 and agreed fact number 30:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Lucy Letby's home address at 41 Westbourne Avenue, Chester was lawfully searched between the 10th and 11 June 2019."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Agreed fact number 31:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Lucy Letby's parents' home address of 13 Arran Avenue, Hereford was lawfully searched between the 10th and 11 June 2019."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: My Lord, I call, please, Colin Johnson.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: DC COLIN JOHNSON (sworn)
Examination-in-chief by MR ASTBURY
Could we begin, please, with you introducing yourself?
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes. Good afternoon, I'm DC Colin Johnson and I am a police officer with Cheshire Police.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is it right that during the course of this investigation you had the specific role of exhibits officer?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That is correct.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Just to deal with that role very briefly, please, so that everybody understands, where exhibits are seized, particularly during the course of a search of, in this case, somebody's home, are they seized by individual officers acting as part of a search team?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that is correct.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: And part of the search team, is this right, is designated as an exhibits officer?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, despatched to a property.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. Not you, in fact, in any of these addresses, as I understand it?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: But the process is then that each exhibit that is seized is then sealed; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: That is signed with a label by the officer who finds it?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's then passed to the nominated exhibits officer at the scene --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: -- who takes responsibility for all exhibits?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: At the scene.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: They are then conveyed by that exhibits officer to a secure location at a police station; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's right.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: A careful log is completed of all exhibits in a particular case?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: They are entered on to a computer system?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: A full log is maintained?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: That log enables an audit trail to be maintained?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: That computer system enables you to maintain a record of any exhibit and its location?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It does.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: And they remain under your supervision, if I can put it that way, until the trial begins?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, they're in a locked room, which myself and (inaudible) have access to.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Sorry, you said things then that I couldn't hear a word of. You said, "In a locked room, which myself", and then something else.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Myself as the exhibits officer has control of that room.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's really important that you speak to the people at the back of the jury --
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Certainly, sorry.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: -- so that everyone can hear what you're saying.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: They're maintained in that locked cupboard but I think since the start of the trial they have been brought to this building; is that right.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: They have.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: And you've continued to maintain their propriety whilst you have been in this trial?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, again in the locked room.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. I'm going to ask you please some general questions about the searches themselves and then specifically certain exhibits. Is it right that we've heard that searches were carried out at two addresses, certainly on 3 July 2018, two domestic addresses?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Also a work location?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: And is it right that a considerable number of exhibits were seized during the course of those searches?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: They were.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: During the course of the searches, did a crime scene investigator attend?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: They did.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did they take photographs of both the scene and various exhibits?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: They did.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did they keep a written record of their conduct at the scene?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: They did.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. In preparation for today have you put together a file, in effect, of images of both the searches and the exhibits themselves?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I have.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm going to ask you, please, you having done that, to take us through the chronology of this particular aspect of the investigation.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Dealing first with the search at 41 Westbourne Avenue in Chester. That search was commenced under a warrant, and therefore lawful, at 06.05 on 3 July 2018; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That is right.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: The search team in fact commenced their activities at 08.50; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: And the address was maintained as a scene, so secure, until the searches concluded at 17.30 hours on 6 July 2018?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It was.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: The officer in charge of the search completed a search record; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: He did.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Part of which was a diagram of the premises itself with each room being given a particular number; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That is correct.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm going to ask Mr Murphy, please, to put image 1 from our file on the screen. We can see there on the left the downstairs of the property; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is correct.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: And on the right-hand side, a representation of the first floor of the property?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: With each bedroom designated a specific number?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: My Lord and members of the jury, the file that we're going to look at appears on the iPad, so I'm not suggesting anybody goes there now, but it can be found in the post-indictment section under "Additional exhibits". I can take everyone back to that in a moment but that's where it's to be found.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Now, I want to deal, please, first with bedroom 1 as it appears on our plan. I'm going to ask Mr Murphy to put up image number 2 on the screen. Is that an image of bedroom 1 as it was found to be that morning?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It was --
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: -- or it is.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: If we can go, please, to image 3. That's the other end of the room, same bed, showing the foot of the bed and furniture in the room?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. I don't want to rush through this if people are looking at the images, but if we move on to image number 4, please. Again, another aspect to the right of the furniture and the foot of the bed and we can see, officer, there if we pause for a moment, a mirror standing alongside the wall; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That is correct.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Amongst the other items we can see on the photograph, to the right of the mirror and on the floor is a dark shape; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Were they in fact two handbags that were located in that particular place?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: They are.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm going to ask Mr Murphy to move on to photograph number 5. We can see there that particularly dark shape in a bit more detail to the right of the mirror.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: If we then go on to photograph 6, please, we see the two handbags there to the right; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: A smaller dark one and a larger burgundy one.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Thank you, Mr Murphy. So that's the location of the two handbags in the room, to the right of the stand-alone mirror against the wall.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Is it right that during the search of the handbag, an officer by the name of PC Clegg recovered three handwritten notes from the handbag?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: He did.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. Were they given the exhibit reference NAC-2?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: So although more than one piece of paper, collectively one exhibit?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Presumably because of the location where they were found?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. You, I think, have provided us with images of those handwritten notes. We'll come to the notes themselves in a moment, but perhaps if we have a look at the images first, please. Photograph number 7, Mr Murphy. They are the three handwritten notes in one image laid out; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: If we go to the next photograph, please. That's a close-up of the yellow Post-it that we saw amongst the three pieces of paper.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Go to the next image, please. That's the other side of the same Post-it; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is, it is.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Hence there being two photographs of them laid out because they're turned over?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, there was writing found on the rear.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. That was my mistake.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Then if we move on again, please, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: My Lord, the jury can see those in a moment, the originals, but just so we can orientate.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's the blue Post-it we saw on the earlier photograph on the handbag; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That is correct.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. And in the next image, writing again on the back of that Post-it, is that correct, officer?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That is correct.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. If we move on again, Mr Murphy. It's a larger piece of paper found within the same handbag.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It was.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: The next image, please. Same piece of paper, reverse side again?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. You helpfully told us that that was given the collective exhibit reference NAC-2.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It was.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Do you have, please, that exhibit to hand?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I do.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. Is this an example of the type of evidence bag that would have been used at the scene itself?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is. It's a standard-issue bag, depending on the size of the exhibit that's required to go into it, which is obviously sealed and the officers sign the front for continuity.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: All three pieces of paper together in there?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: They are.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think we probably need to open the bag, please.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Can you identify them formally please as NAC-2?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Certainly.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. If you put them back in the bag. Now the bag is opened, I'm going to ask that the jury have a look at those, please. My Lord may want to see those first.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: (Pause)

I've said to you several times now anything that is exhibited is an exhibit in the case and you can look at it any time. If you started trying to read these, you can take a very long time for you individually to look at them, so may I suggest at this stage -- are there going to be any...?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: The image that is we have on the screen will be available on the iPad and they can be zoomed in and out.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: We really get the impression of the documents rather than just -- the yellow and blue ones are Post-it notes, obviously.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (Pause)
I'll talk over while this is going on. Just in relation -- are they on the iPad yet or not?
Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: So which baby do we go into to get them?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Go to the list of babies. After [Baby Q] we'll find "Postindictment" as a separate file.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: So it's in the post-indictment section?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes. If one enters that, it's on the additional button to the right, by SoE, and then there's "additional".
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (Pause)
My Lord, we've taken, by example, the yellow Post-it note and enlarged it on the screen. Some of the writing is easier to read than others, but there's some of the examples that are contained within.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I'm going to go on, by way of introduction, next then, please, to image 18, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's a diary from 2016, so it's the diary we'll be introducing next, please. By way of introduction, can we go, please, to image number 15.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: We've looked already, officer, at the chest of drawers at the foot of the bed. Is it right that the diary we've just looked at was found during the search of the middle set of the chest of drawers that we can see against the wall?
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: That is correct.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. It was PC Clegg again, as I understand it, correct me if I'm wrong, who seized the diary from the top drawer of that middle chest of drawers; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That is correct.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Obviously, the diary contained a number of pages and I think a full PDF copy was made of each and every page; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It was.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: I want to just look, please, with you at two of those particular pages. Image 16, please, from that diary.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: If we can enlarge it a little bit, please, Mr Murphy, if that's possible, so we can see the dates clearly.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's April, as we know, of 2016. We can see on 8 April, which was, the jury will recall, the date of birth of [Babies L & M], the twins, we can see an entry "LD" and "twins".
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: We can.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: If we zoom out and look at Saturday, 9 April, which is a date that features on the indictment. We can see an entry:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "LD (extra) twin resus."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: For the sake of completeness, under that particular entry on the same date, "Salsa and book group"; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: We can.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. As I say, all of the pages were imaged and have been provided, but can I take you next to image number 17.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Before we do that, I think the image of the diary on that date should be exhibit 12, that particular page.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It's easier just to exhibit the diary, my Lord, and the image will be there that's relevant. Perhaps if I can scrub that suggestion and come back to it in a moment.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think -- otherwise we're going to end up with an awful lot of exhibit numbers for perhaps little purpose.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I agree, thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: So looking at this particular date in June of 2016, could I invite, please, Mr Murphy just to look at 23 June 2016, which was a Thursday. We can see, I'll be corrected if I'm wrong, it looks like "LD" again and in brackets a "[redacted]"; is that correct.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that is correct.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: The jury will recall that was the date upon which, sadly, [Baby O] died.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Then on the 24th, the following day, we can see "LD"
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: again and "[redacted]", that being the date, I observe, that [Baby P] passed away.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: And a reference "A + E", which I think we've also heard a little bit about as well.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: If we can zoom out again, please, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: If we go to the 25th on the top of the next page we can see "LD" and "[redacted]".
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: We can.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. The jury will recall that was the date upon which the Crown allege [Baby Q] was attacked.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So they're two selected pages from the diary. Can I ask, do you have the diary with you now?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I do.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm going to ask you, to save exhibiting it any other way, that we exhibit that as exhibit number 12, please.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: (Pause)
If we could go back to image 18 again, please, Mr Murphy.

That's the image we've looked at of the diary already, but I'd like to focus next, please, on the Post-it that we can see on the right on the picture. Is it right that that was found inside the diary?
Yes.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Again, seized by PC Clegg?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: And on this occasion, given its own separate exhibit reference of NAC-10?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It was.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. I'm going to ask -- we've already heard about this Post-it note, albeit some time ago. I'm going to ask Mr Murphy to enlarge it, please, if possible, and perhaps look at the top half to begin with.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: (Pause)
Officer, are you able to produce, please, the original Post-it taken from the diary?
I can.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. You may want to leave it in the bags so it doesn't get lost. That's NAC-10, that's the original, and that will be exhibit 13 for the court record, please.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Do you want the jury to see this or not?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Very quickly. It's clearer on the screen.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I was going to say, you won't be able to read it. It's only written on one side and you have it.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Do you want to look at it? No?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you. If we can move on, please, Mr Murphy, to image number 20.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: This is another piece of paper that was found inside the diary; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: This is a A4-sized piece of paper. You can see the type of writing on it. Perhaps if Mr Murphy can zoom in on the top portion.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Are you able, please, to produce that particular piece of paper --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can.
blocks.speaker: DC JOHNSON

blocks.text: -- as KLF-4?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Perhaps if we pause while everyone has a look at the document.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's one side of it, but there's another side.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: (Pause)
If I could ask Mr Murphy to scroll down to the next part.
We have both sides, my Lord, one of each.
(Pause)
Thank you. If we move down, Mr Murphy, please.
(Pause)
There's a crossed-out box, which might not be as clear. I'm going to ask to zoom in on that, please, to the left of the page.
(Pause)
Next page, please.

blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.

blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.

blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, no problem.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: The interview begins with introductions and caution.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: The caution is a formal set of words at the outset of an interview; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Can you confirm for me that it is as follows:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "You don't have to say anything but it may harm your defence if you fail to mention when questioned something that you later rely on in court, and anything you do say may be given in evidence"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Thank you. The introductions consist of everybody stating their name who's present?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And an outline of what's about to take place?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Then the first question:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Do you understand that Lucy"; yes?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Lucy Letby then confirmed that she'd received a copy of her notes relating to [Baby A].
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Okay. In relation to [Baby A], other than the notes, do you remember [Baby A] and your care of [Baby A], other than the notes you've just gone through?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: You do. Would you like to tell me exactly, in your own words then, what your involvement was with [Baby A] regarding around the time he collapsed?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So I remember I came on duty -- we start our night shift at 7.30 and we have a general handover period which usually lasts until around 8 o'clock. And at that point I went to [Baby A]'s cot side to receive individual handover with the nurse that had been looking after him in the day -- and I believe this was around 8 o'clock and at this point the nurse looking after him was connecting or drawing up some fluids to be connected via a long line that [Baby A] had inserted during the day.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So at this point, whilst we were getting -- sorry, so while at this point, whilst we were getting handover from each other, I checked the fluids with this other nurse and she connected them via the long line and shortly after that is when we noticed that [Baby A] had gone quite pale and mottled in his skin. Dave Harkness, the registrar, was in the nursery at the time and we called Dave over and began initiating airway support because [Baby A] was apnoeic and then we put a crash call out and Dr Jayaram came and then [Baby A] had full resuscitation.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: You came on duty at 7.30?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So what was your -- what were your actions when you came on duty on the ward?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So we have a generalised handover to start with all the nursing colleagues that hand over from the day shift to the night shift.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: And then, I'm not 100% sure of the timing, but I believe I got to [Baby A]'s cot side around 8 o'clock to have individual handover on [Baby A] from the nurse that was caring.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Do you specifically remember this shift with [Baby A]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. What -- why do you remember that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I remember [Baby A].
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So do you specifically recall going to [Baby A]'s cot side?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Tell us about your observations of [Baby A] at that time.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So I remember [Baby A] was on CPAP, which is respiratory support, and I didn't have a lot to do with [Baby A] at that time because when I came to get handover the nurse caring for him was already drawing
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: up sterile fluids to go through the long line that had just been put in by the doctors, so we went straight to checking the fluids.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Tell me about what the support was, the breathing support?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: [Baby A] was receiving CPAP.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. And at that point was there anything that alerted you to anything, even though you can't remember which specifically [Baby A] had? Did you notice anything that concerned you with the way he was receiving that treatment?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Not with that. The only thing I do remember is that he was a little bit jittery in appearance. He was a bit jittery in his limbs and that can be a sign of low blood sugars, and he was due a blood gas and a blood sugar shortly after I came on shift.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So tell me what jittery is?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Jittery is sort of when the baby is making sort of involuntary jerking movements, their limbs.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So it's not in reaction to pain?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: No. So it --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Jittering is something you recognise as being -- it can be a sign of low blood sugar, it's quite a different movement.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Is that common?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is common for preterm babies to be hypoglycaemic, yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And was that --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: And that's why we were keen to get the fluids connected because we were conscious that he hadn't had fluids via his long line in the UVC at that point.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Would the fluids have included something that would aid the jitteriness?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. And what was that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I'm not sure without looking which fluids we connected, whether it's 10% glucose or TPN.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So tell me who the nurse was that you took over from.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Melanie Taylor.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. What was her hand over to you? This is from memory.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't remember specific details.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: But I don't recall there being anything of any due concern.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Then the other officer asks:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "So when you came on duty how was [Baby A] presenting to you initially?"
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: From what I remember he -- I didn't have any concerns other than this jittery movement.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Do you remember how long into your shift that he became jittery?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So you said you that checked the fluids with the other nurse. Is that again something that you specifically remember with regards to [Baby A]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't remember which fluids, but I know that Mel was there with the fluids when I came to get handover and we made that a priority, to check the fluids and get those set up and running.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Again, why was that -- why was that a priority?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Because he hadn't had his cannula, his peripheral cannula inserted in the day. He'd had a UVC that they weren't happy to use and he'd had a long line inserted that the doctors had confirmed we could use. So I think he'd gone a few hours without any fluids.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Is that normal? Is that a cause for concern?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It's not ideal but when you have new babies and it's -- you have -- you can have problems obtaining access to be able to give fluids, yeah.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right, okay. But there was nothing that gave you concern apart from the jitteriness --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, not that I remember.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: -- at the point of handover?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So you said he became pale and mottled. Is that during the handover with Melanie?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think it was after we connected the fluids.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: He -- he was normal in appearance when we were having handover and once we connected the fluids, it was noted that he -- his colour changed.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So with regards, again from memory, yourself and Melanie, did you do that together?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think Mel was drawing up the fluids and Mel was sterile because you have to do it aseptically, connecting fluids, so I believe she was gowned up and setting the fluids up and I checked the fluids with her because two people have to check any bags or any fluids that were running.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: And then I think, from memory, Mel connected the fluids to the long line.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So what --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: And then we set up the pump together, the infusion pump.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So physical interaction at that stage with [Baby A], what exactly did you do --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't --
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: -- in layman's terms?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't recall having any physical contact with [Baby A] at that point.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So when did you have physical contact with [Baby A]; do you recall?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No. I think it was when he deteriorated.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: And then the other officer:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Do you remember what you were doing just prior to the deterioration, Lucy, what -- where you were?"
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think I was at the bedside checking the equipment. So usually when we have received handover we'll then go through and check all the emergency equipment.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Check any infusion pumps, any ventilator support, you check all the equipment, check your incubator, those sorts of things.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And were there any issues with the equipment at that time?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. And that's where you were just before he became unwell?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, I think so.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Was anyone else there with you at the time?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So Mel was still in the room and a registrar, Dave Harkness, was in the room with [Baby B].
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. What was Mel doing, do you remember, at the time?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Were there any other babies?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think she may have been writing her notes, but I -- I'm not 100% sure.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right. Were there any other babies in the room at that time?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I know [Baby B] was in the room. I'm not sure about any others.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right. Who was [Baby B]'s nurse at the time?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think it was Caroline Bennion but again I'm not certain. I know Caroline Bennion was there because she became involved once [Baby A] deteriorated. I'm not sure if she was on the day shift or the night shift.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And you say Dr Harkness was there?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: What was he doing then?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: He was doing something with [Baby B]. I'm not sure. But I just remember him being at her incubator.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right. Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Then the officer:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Okay. So you've done those kind of connections. You didn't have any concerns at that stage. How long between doing those and you noticing [Baby A] becoming pale and mottled?"
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It was fairly soon. Within minutes, I think.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: 30 minutes, 2 minutes?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't know. Maybe 5 minutes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Something like that.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And Melanie had moved on to doing her notes?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think so.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And you were doing the check of the equipment?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So tell me how you interpret pale first of all in a neonatal baby?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It's a loss of colour. Babies are usually quite pink and he'd become more pale, as in almost white.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. What does that mean to you as a nurse in that field?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That there's something wrong.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Like what?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It could be an infection.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Could it be they are hypoglycaemic, that they've had a sudden collapse?
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. And mottled, the same thing, how do you interpret the mottled appearance?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So mottled is a bit more of -- almost like a rash appearance, like blotchy red marks on the skin.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Is that a reflection of something in your experience?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Again, it can be a sign of infection, low blood sugars.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: If they're cold they can become mottled. If they've got poor blood gases.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. And exactly what is mottled?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: What is a mottled appearance?
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So when the baby's quite pale and white and they can have sort of red areas on them.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Red?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yeah, like reddy-purple, yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Was this specifically with regards to [Baby A], was it localised or was it spread out? Where exactly did the mottling appear?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think it was his hands and feet.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: And he was centrally pale.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So those two together, considering how he presented to you at that time, what were your actions then?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So I think I went to him and checked him and found that he was apnoeic and not breathing.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So how did you check him, what do you mean by check?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I looked to see if he was breathing and if the CPAP mask was in place still and the machine was running.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And was it?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Which machine was running?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: The CPAP machine.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay, yeah.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: And then straightaway Dave was in the room, Dave Harkness, and I called him over from what I recall.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. How did -- did you have to almost stimulate [Baby A] or physically check him?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think so but I can't remember.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And then Lucy Letby described the initial steps that would usually be taken to stimulate an apnoeic baby.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: And the officer asked: Okay, so you say that, you saw he wasn't breathing, that he was apnoeic.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So tell me how that presented in [Baby A].
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: How did I know that he was apnoeic?
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think I went over and assessed him. He wasn't breathing and I'm not sure what his observations were doing. I can't recall his observations at the time.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. And then the other officer:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "At that time, was anyone else with you?"
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, Dave Harkness was on the cot side next to him. I'm sure Mel was in the room and Caroline Bennion.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So Dave Harkness would have witnessed the apnoea, the breathing had stopped, yeah?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I'm not sure that he was looking at [Baby A] at that time, but he was in the room.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So how did he become aware that [Baby A] was apnoeic?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: We called him over.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Who's we?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I'm not sure whether it was myself or Mel or Caroline.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I'm not sure who. We were all in the room from what I remember, so I'm not sure which of us -- who I called for first -- or how it -- we were all in close proximity.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Was he attached to any monitors?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, he would have been attached to a Philips monitor.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So in [Baby A]'s case in particular, was the monitor -did the monitor go off?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't remember --
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: -- specifically.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Was it the monitors that attracted you to [Baby A] being apnoeic or was it your visual observations?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't recall but I would assume it would be the monitor.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So had you moved away from [Baby A] after you'd done the handover?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't specifically -- I don't know.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right. Because you said you were checking the --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: If the equipment is adjacent to the cot side though --
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Yeah, so were you during that period of handover to you seeing/making these observations of the collapse?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Sorry. I'm not sure that makes sense.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Were you with [Baby A] throughout that period?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I believe I was checking the equipment, yes, at his cot side and his charts.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: When you talk about this mottled rash, can you give us any further description of how it showed, its shape?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think from memory it was more on the side that had his line in.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Which side was that, do you remember?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think it was his left.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. And you described it as a red/purple colour.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Can you sort of help us with any comparisons with anything colour-wise, the way it showed? Was there any -- was it bright red, was it dark red?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think it was more pale than the mottling, than the little areas of the mottling.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: But predominantly it was paleness.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Did anyone else see that mottling on [Baby A]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, I think it was still there when I called Dave and Caroline and the other nursing staff came in.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Did they say anything about it to you?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, we were advised to stop the fluids on the long line straightaway.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Did they say what they thought it was?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think Dave mentioned that it could be potentially an issue with the line, so to stop the fluids.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: The other officer:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "How does a long line cause mottling?"
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: If a long line wasn't in the correct position you were running fluids and it was going outside of the bloodstream into the tissues then it would cause circulatory problems to --
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay, right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: -- that limb or that area.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Who had inserted the long line?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think it was Dave Harkness. Doctors insert it, so it would have been a member of the medical team.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. And that was prior to you coming on duty, I think you said, didn't you?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Because -- so that was already in situ?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And Lucy Letby was then asked to explain some of the entries from the notes which with she'd been provided.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: The officer says: Okay at 20.05 you put, "10% glucose commenced via long line with SN Taylor as agreed by Registrar Harkness, who was present."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: My Lord, that's a reference to tile 175 on the [Baby A] interview. I don't know whether it would help to have that up now so the jury know what's being discussed. 175.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: The question is: What was this for?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: All the babies that aren't being fed need to have some fluids running to maintain the blood sugars, so 10% glucose is the standard formula we would give for TPN.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So [Baby A] was commenced on, obviously, 10% glucose.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. And if we move along there I think we've covered -- you noted him to be jittery, that he was due to have a blood gas and blood sugar taken. I think you mentioned that to us, didn't you? And you went through the process of that. How was [Baby A] handling at that time?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't recall handling [Baby A].
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right. At all that day?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Then I think you've put at 20.20, "[Baby A]'s hands and feet needed to be wiped. Centrally pale, poor perfusion, [Baby A] became apnoeic."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: This is tile 179. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So you put there that [Baby A] became apnoeic at the time, his hands and feet were noticeably white. So is that -- was that the correct sort of way it sort of displayed: his hands and feet were white, you saw them being white and then he became apnoeic at the same time or was that afterwards?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't recall specifically.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: But was anyone else present when you saw those?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: There were other staff present in the nursery, yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Then she went on --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I remember raising about them being white. That's when I was advised to stop the fluids.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: At that time?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, I believe when I was -- called for help, yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So where you've put "centrally pale and perfusion", the poor perfusion refers to how you described around the --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: The limbs, yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: The extremities, okay?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. And that could be caused [by a] problem with the long line?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So that's the same thing?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Then the other officer:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "What do you mean by perfusion then? What's perfusion?"
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: The circulation.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Was there a reason why it was particularly poor with [Baby A] --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: -- in your opinion?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Then you've got Registrar Harkness in the nursery and assistance called for, so I take it he was there pretty straightaway, was he?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And what was his initial advice to you?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: To stop the fluids.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And then shortly afterwards -- afterwards, "No heart rate was detected and full resuscitation commenced as per the medical notes". Do you want to just go through that process of the resuscitation for us then? Your, involvement?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: And then:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Specifically to [Baby A], to [Baby A]."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Okay. I can't remember specifically my role with [Baby A].
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right. Is there anything at all that you do remember about the resuscitation?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Then sadly, [Baby A] passed away at 20.58 hours and was given to the parents to cuddle. How were you feeling about that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It was awful, really.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Can you explain what was going through your mind?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Just how quickly it had all happened and I didn't have a relationship with the parents or anything and obviously they came and [Baby B] was in the room at the time and we were conscious that we were split between two babies and [Baby B] was present when this was all happening as well.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Do you know who gave -- gave him to the parents, who passed [Baby A]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think it was myself.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: You think or you remember?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, I can't remember specifically for definite.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: What made you think it might have been you?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Usually it's the member of staff that has cared for the baby that's assigned to look after the baby that would have that role.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: It must be a very difficult time for you.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: How do you sort of deal with that? What's your sort of coping mechanism for that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think we just all as a team sort of supported one an other with it.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Do you remember any sort of debriefs or chats with --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: There was a debrief.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Debrief?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: A few days later, I think. I'm not sure of the exact date but there was one held formally.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: You remember that, do you?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Who was involved with that? Who was present?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think it was led by Dr Jayaram. I can't remember any of the specific details about it.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Was there any particular outcome from it at all?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, I believe there was some mention that mum had various health issues that were looking into, whether they could have affected [Baby A] and [Baby B], but I don't recall anything else.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: What about offloading to friends or family, you know, after your shift? Did you do any of that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't remember specifically but I would have told my parents and my friends, yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: But you don't know specifically?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Then presumably this is to the other officer: Is there anything you want to ask?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: The officer says:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Up to [Baby A] had you had experience of babies passing away professionally prior to his death?"
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. What kind of occasions were they, in what circumstances?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I'd seen babies pass away at Liverpool Women's when I was doing my training there, very pre-term babies.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: And I -- we lost a 23-week baby on the unit when I first started, so I'd seen that baby.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Is there sometimes an element of a death being expected within the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Sometimes, yes --
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: -- depending on the baby's condition and gestation and things, yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: With regards to [Baby A], was his death anticipated or expected?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No. My concern at the time was whether there was -- had been any issue with the long line because it was sort of in a few minutes after we connected the fluids that he seemed to deteriorate, so I think my concern was that there was an issue either with the line or the fluids that we'd connected.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So you explained about how the long line can be in the wrong position and that can cause problems. So that was your concern with the long line; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. What are the -- what were your concerns about the fluids that had been administered and could cause a collapse?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So I didn't have a concern specifically about the fluid, but when thinking of what could have caused it my concern was maybe the bag of fluid wasn't what we thought it was potentially.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: And then the other officer:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "What did you think it was?"
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: 10% glucose.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Did you say that Melanie attached it or you just don't recall who attached it?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I believe Mel was sterile so I think Mel would have attached it if she was sterile.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: She would have been the one to have connected it.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: I can't remember for definite who connected the bag, no.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Where does the bag come from?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So the bags are all pre-sealed and they're in a cupboard in nursery 1.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So who actually retrieves those out of the cupboard?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: The nursing staff.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay so did you retrieve that bag for [Baby A]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, not that I recall. I recall that Mel already had the bag out --
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: -- and was -- and already had the line ready to run through, so we checked the bag together.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. As part of your checks of the -- his equipment did you recheck his bag and the long line after Mel had attached it?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't recall specifically.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Would there be any record made of who attached this bag?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So usually when we sign the drug chart, the signature that signed for first is usually the person that connected and the signature below is the co-signer.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: For the next part of the interview the officer returned to the notes and as a result of which asked this:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "You then go on to say that:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The hand and footprints were taken with consent along with a lock of hair. Hand and footprints of sibling also obtained as per parents' wishes. Parents and maternal and paternal grandparents have had time alone cuddling [Baby A]. [Baby A] has also spent time on CLS with parents on cold cot. Photos taken with unit camera and parents' phones."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: My Lord, I don't need to go to it now but the reference for that note is tile 222: Do you remember who did those activities?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I believe I did. The footprints, I remember doing those for [Baby B].
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Can you go through the process of how you would do that then?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: We have a set, a kit on the unit, that has a set of paper and wipes that we wipe the foot with and then imprint that on to a piece of card and that's usually done with two people. We do it with the hand and the feet.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Obviously a very difficult -- [Baby A]'s passed away and you're doing that. How does it make you feel doing that process?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I personally find that process quite -- it's quite nice to do something nice for the baby and with the baby and I see it as a way of giving parents memories.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Where did they take place? Where do you actually do this?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't remember specifically where we do it but you can either do it in the incubator or after the baby's passed away and it's on the cold cot, we can do it in there.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: We can do it when they're sat on the mum and dad.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: We can do it wherever, really. I don't recall specifically where I did [Baby A]'s.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And is -- who is present when this occurred?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Anybody can be present. So if -- the parents can be there. We usually do it with two members of staff for the practicality of having somebody to assist you with the paper and the wipes, so it's usually two members of staff do it.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And what -- the documentation that you refer to in those notes — what is that documentation?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So we have a bereavement checklist that we have to go through when a baby dies. So we tick things that we've done, such as hand and footprints, if photographs have been taken, is the baby labelled, do parents -- aware of things like that, and that's passed over then to the staff taking over and they continue that sheet.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Lucy Letby was then asked about a reference to [Baby A]'s parents in her notes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: The question was posed: Is there a reason why you refer to them as mummy and daddy? Can you see that within those notes?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Because they are their mum and dad.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Obviously, some people call them by their names or parents of. But the reason why you --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, usually we would refer to them as mum and dad or parents. We don't usually name them by their Christian names.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Then you put mementos gathered and placed in a memory box. Why was this done?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's what we'd do for any baby that's passed away.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: We have a set bereavement box with various mementos in it and that's when we would put things like the hand and footprints and items from their cots, such as their cot card, their name bands.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: What about the family? Did you ever keep in touch with the family after [Baby A] died?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Only whilst [Baby B] was still a patient on the unit.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Did you make any other notes through the course of caring for [Baby A], did you make any other notes before you placed those on to the system?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't recall specifically with [Baby A], but quite often we have a handover sheet where we write down information about the baby and if he was having a resus event or anything like that, you might make notes on the back of your handover sheet to use at the end of the day to help with writing your notes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. You know the notes that you do make, handwritten notes that you make, like you say, for the purpose of handover, what happens to those at the end of the shift?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: They're usually disposed then in confidential waste.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right, okay. What do you do with yours? What did you do with [Baby A]'s in particular?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't recall.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: A discussion then took place regarding shift rotas at the time. A file, we are told, was kept on the unit with shifts planned around a month in advance. Any swaps with other members of staff or overtime would be handwritten on the paper forms. And there was no electronic system for clocking on and off. Then Lucy Letby was asked: How do you actually get on to the unit?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It's swipe access --
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: -- to gain entry to the unit.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay, and are there any particular times where you would work more overtime or times when you wouldn't want to, you know, do you have set holidays throughout the year?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. You don't get a call like last minute, 'We're short of staff'?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yeah.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: You do?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: How often was that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Quite frequently on sort of a week-to-week basis, I would say.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So what sort of notice would you be given for the overtime?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I mean, sometimes they would call you in the morning and say, "Could you work tonight?" or ring you today and say, "Would you be able to work tomorrow?"
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Do you remember anybody else giving [Baby A] care in between the time that you had the handover and the point of his collapse? I think you said about 8.20.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Obviously, having -- obviously, you've had his notes. Having read his notes, do you think there was anything that you need to raise for us to have a look at during this interview now with regards to [Baby A] that you feel we need to discuss?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Then Ms Letby's solicitor spoke: The thing is in relation to [Baby A], I think you've only had less 20 minutes contact with him in total, is that --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And then reverting to the officer: Yeah, including his parents. Ever?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that was the first time.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: From the time of coming on duty to the time --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That was the first time I've met [Baby A], yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So within the 20 minutes that you had, he's gone downhill, he became pale, you saw this mottled effect on the feet, apnoeic, stopped breathing, collapsed, and then obviously a full resuscitation attempt was made.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Is that a fair sort of summary of what happened with [Baby A]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Is there anything else you would like to tell us about [Baby A] and your care for [Baby A] that can help us with this investigation?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No. So the only concern that I had was there was an issue potentially with the line or the fluid that we'd attached.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. And again, we've spoken about the line: the potential problem there was that it was wrongly located and that whatever was put through the line would seep out of the bloodstream?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Yeah, and the other potential problem there is the bag and whether it contained the correct prescription?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And the interview in respect of [Baby A] was concluded at that point.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Thank you. I'll just make this point, my Lord, if I may. Often, an interview would carry on to another baby, it wouldn't necessarily stop and then start another interview.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Yes, but as has been done throughout this case, it's all been compartmentalised, so the interviews will be specific to the individual babies.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes. Is that an appropriate point?
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: That gives you an idea of what's to come and another file of this. All right? These are your paper copies, your working documents for such use as you wish to put them during the course of the trial. We will now break
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: off because there's no point in starting another interview and we will resume on Wednesday because tomorrow is a day off.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Friday is a day off. Monday the 24th is a day off and Wednesday the 26th is a day off so far as April is concerned. I will give you the full list on Wednesday in relation to it, but as far as this week is concerned, as you know, not sitting tomorrow, so it's Wednesday and Thursday of this week that you're required.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Next week, you're required Tuesday, Thursday and Friday. All right? You should have that in a sheet of paper that you had from earlier, before the Easter break. Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Please remember your solemn responsibilities as jurors in this case: no communication by any means with anyone, no research about anything to do with this case.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: You'll see we've already got seven non-sitting days in May. So I'm not saying anything further at this stage, but we're just going to have to consider what's going to be done. That's why I didn't go beyond April with them.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Ms Letby is being brought tomorrow, is she?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, we understand she is, and we're grateful for that. We'd be grateful just for the opportunity for a brief visit at the end of today, at the conclusion today.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I can see the officer is nodding.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS
